description: Conducting an authorised penetration test end to end: rules of engagement and the law, open-source and active reconnaissance, scanning and enumeration, exploitation and password attacks, post-exploitation and privilege escalation, and reporting findings with remediation. Practised only against isolated virtual machines and simulated networks in the browser, with every exercise scoped and authorised so techniques are learned lawfully.
modelledOn: Weidman, Penetration Testing: A Hands-On Introduction to Hacking
Engebretson, The Basics of Hacking and Penetration Testing
OWASP Testing Guide and NIST SP 800-115
outcomes: Scope an engagement and work within rules of engagement, authorisation and the relevant law.
Gather intelligence on a target with open-source and active reconnaissance.
Scan and enumerate hosts, services and versions to build an attack surface map.
Exploit vulnerabilities and crack passwords against authorised lab targets.
Escalate privilege, move laterally and establish persistence during post-exploitation.
Write a clear penetration test report that prioritises findings and recommends remediation.

units.title: Rules of engagement and the law
topics: Why authorisation is everything: the line between a penetration test and a crime
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act 2020 and Data Protection Act 843; the Cyber Security Authority and lawful disclosure
Scoping: targets, exclusions, time windows, permitted techniques and emergency contacts
Rules of engagement, get-out-of-jail letters, data handling and confidentiality
Penetration testing methodologies and standards; types of test: black, grey and white box
Professional ethics and responsible disclosure

units.title: The tester's environment
topics: Building an isolated lab of virtual machines and a simulated network in the browser
A testing distribution and its toolchain; keeping test traffic off production
Note-taking, evidence capture and command logging for a defensible report
Networking refresher: addressing, ports, protocols and the OSI layers as they matter to testing

units.title: Reconnaissance
topics: Passive open-source intelligence: WHOIS, DNS records, certificate transparency, search and social media
Footprinting an organisation: employees, technologies, leaked credentials and metadata
Active reconnaissance and when passive crosses into active
Mapping the external attack surface, including exposed mobile-money and SIM-registration portals
Organising findings into a target profile

units.title: Scanning and enumeration
topics: Host discovery and port scanning with nmap; scan types, timing and evasion basics
Service and version detection and operating-system fingerprinting
Vulnerability scanning with OpenVAS and interpreting results without over-trusting them
Enumerating services: web, SMB, SNMP, SMTP, DNS and databases
Turning scan output into a prioritised list of likely entry points

units.title: Exploitation
topics: From vulnerability to working exploit; matching a service version to a known flaw and CVE/CVSS
Using an exploitation framework: payloads, listeners and sessions
Common server-side flaws: unpatched services, default credentials, misconfigurations
Client-side and social-engineering vectors in a controlled lab
Verifying impact without damaging the target; avoiding denial of service

units.title: Password attacks
topics: Where credentials live: hashes, caches, configuration files and memory
Online attacks: brute force, dictionary, spraying and credential stuffing against lab services
Offline cracking of captured hashes with John the Ripper and hashcat; wordlists and rules
Default and reused passwords; the weakness of SMS one-time codes and SIM-swap risk
Defences: strong hashing, lockout, multi-factor authentication

units.title: Post-exploitation
topics: Local situational awareness after a foothold: users, processes, network and stored secrets
Privilege escalation on Linux and Windows: misconfigurations, weak permissions, kernel and service flaws
Lateral movement and pivoting through a simulated internal network
Persistence, and the difference between a test artefact and real-world stealth
Collecting proof of access and cleaning up afterwards

units.title: Web and network attack techniques
topics: Web application testing against the OWASP Top Ten: injection, broken authentication, access control
Intercepting proxies and request manipulation with Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP
Network attacks in the lab: sniffing, spoofing and man-in-the-middle
Wireless assessment basics against a simulated access point

units.title: Reporting findings
topics: Structure of a penetration test report: executive summary, methodology, findings, evidence
Rating severity with likelihood and impact; CVSS as an input, not the whole story
Writing actionable remediation that a stretched IT team in a cafe or school can apply
Re-testing and verifying fixes; the debrief
Capstone: a full authorised test of a simulated small-business network and a written report
